Q: SQL Server GROUP BY too slow A:

I would suggest you below approaches to solve the performance problem:

  1. Try to create a composite non-clustered index on Company, Department in the base table of the view, to give good performance for GROUP BY.
  2. As you are not able to create index on the view, try to create one more view which is having the columns: Company, Department, company_id, action_id, report_Date, with GROUP BY applied already and it should be possible for you index this view, as it is straightforward view. Just query the view with filters applied.

Q: How to make tables with relationships in SQLAlchemy in different files A:

The problem is that when SQLAlchemy initializes TableA, it tries to resolve the string "tablec" to the association table, but that class hasn't been imported or registered with the Base metadata yet. All three models need to be registered with the same Base before any mapper initialization happens.

The fix is to make sure all your model files are imported before you use any of them. The cleanest way to do this is to create an __init__.py (or a models.py barrel file) that imports all models in the correct order:

# database/models/__init__.py

from database.models.base import Base
from database.models.tablec import TableC   # association table first
from database.models.tablea import TableA
from database.models.tableb import TableB

Then wherever you need to use your models or create tables, always import from that package rather than from individual files:

from database.models import Base, TableA, TableB

This ensures that by the time SQLAlchemy resolves the string references like "tablec", all three classes have already been registered against Base.metadata.

A couple of things to keep in mind. First, make sure all three model files import Base from the same single location. If you accidentally create two different Base = declarative_base() calls, the models won't share a registry and the resolution will still fail. Second, for the association table in a many-to-many relationship, you can alternatively define it as a plain Table object rather than a full ORM class, which is actually the more common SQLAlchemy pattern:

# database/models/tablec.py
from database.models.base import Base
from sqlalchemy import Column, ForeignKey, Table

tablec = Table(
    "tablec",
    Base.metadata,
    Column("tablea_id", ForeignKey("tablea.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), primary_key=True),
    Column("tableb_id", ForeignKey("tableb.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), primary_key=True),
)

With this approach, when you pass secondary="tablec" as a string in your relationships, SQLAlchemy looks it up in Base.metadata.tables by table name, and it will find it as long as the module defining tablec has been imported first.

The core takeaway is that string-based resolution in SQLAlchemy relationships only works if all referenced models and tables have been imported and registered before the mappers are configured. A central __init__.py that imports everything in order is the standard solution for multi-file model setups.

Q: Getting Laravel Spatie Permissions - ExpressionChangedAfterItHasBeenCheckedError A:

I fixed my Issue with adding following in my @Component:

@Component({
  selector: 'app-dashboard',
  imports: [MatTabsModule],
  templateUrl: './dashboard.html',
  styleUrl: './dashboard.scss',
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
})
export class Dashboard {

So basically what changeDetection onPush does, is that it tells Angular not to re-check this component on every change-detection. Instead Angular updates the component only when:

  • an @Input() value changes
  • an event happens like (click)
  • an async source used in template emits
  • or if we manually request a check like markForCheck()

I found this solution in another stackoverflow post.

For this solution, I had to add adapt following code
  • Import:
    • import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, ChangeDetectorRef } from '@angular/core';
  • in Class:
    • private cdr = inject(ChangeDetectorRef);
  • in getAllPerms():
    • this.allPermissions = res; this.cdr.markForCheck();
